recent_posts.title: DIY galvanic electrolysis machine built with RP2040 for permanent hair removal
recent_posts.summary: A maker built a DIY galvanic electrolysis machine for permanent hair removal using an RP2040 microcontroller, a 3.7V lithium battery with a boost converter to 15V, an OLED display, rotary encoder, foot pedal, and a DAC/op-amp/MOSFET circuit for precise current control. The project started with a crude 12V car battery setup and evolved into a polished device with a custom PCB and 3D-printed housing. Hardware files are available on GitLab. The build offers a low-cost alternative to expensive professional electrolysis treatments.

recent_posts.title: 2026 Green Powered Challenge winners announced
recent_posts.summary: Hackaday announces the winners of the 2026 Green Powered Challenge, a contest for self-sustaining, environmentally-powered hardware hacks. Three main winners each receive a $150 DigiKey shopping spree: LightInk Solar Watch (an ESP32 e-ink watch that halves power consumption by running screen updates in the RTC wakeup stub), Supercapacitor Solar IoT (a solar supercapacitor charger with boost converter for stable IoT power), and powerTimer (an ultra-low quiescent power latching switch module). Honorable mentions cover solar dev boards, a gravity-powered clock, NFC energy harvesting for microcontroller wakeup, and a human-powered generator bike that has produced 38 kWh over five years.

recent_posts.title: Wigglegrams With A Pinhole Camera
recent_posts.summary: A 3D-printed dual pinhole camera design that takes 4"x5" photographic paper and features two side-by-side cameras in a single body. In landscape orientation it functions as a pair of panoramic cameras; in portrait mode it becomes a stereo camera capable of producing wigglegrams. The design uses magnetic shutters and thumbscrew-attached lid. The creator is considering releasing the STL files.

recent_posts.title: Global satellite navigation systems beyond GPS explained
recent_posts.summary: A broad overview of the world's satellite navigation systems beyond GPS. Covers GLONASS (Russia), BeiDou (China), Galileo (EU), QZSS (Japan), and NavIC (India) — including their histories, orbital designs, accuracy levels, and current operational status. Highlights how multi-system receivers benefit from interoperability across all constellations.

recent_posts.title: University Of Utah’s TRIGA Research Reactor Set To Produce Electricity
recent_posts.summary: The University of Utah's TRIGA research reactor, installed in 1975, is set to generate electricity for the first time in a world's first demonstration. Startup Elemental Nuclear is installing a closed Brayton cycle helium-based generator that will produce 2-3 kWe from the reactor's 50 kWth output. The proof-of-concept aims to validate TRIGA-based microreactor technology for powering AI data centers, potentially opening a path to small nuclear reactors as datacenter power sources.

recent_posts.title: NHK World's Texico teaches programming concepts to kids without a computer
recent_posts.summary: NHK World's Texico program teaches core programming concepts to children without using a computer. Using physical props like toy trains and playing cards, the ten-episode series (available in English and French) covers ideas such as analysis, abstraction, simulation, and algorithms. Real-world examples like mail sorting and fireworks packing illustrate algorithmic thinking in everyday contexts.

recent_posts.title: FPGA board runs 10240 oscillators for hardware Fourier audio synthesis
recent_posts.summary: A hardware project cramming 10,240 individually controllable oscillators onto a Terasic DE10-nano FPGA board. Rather than traditional voice-based polyphony, the creator built a 'spectrum engine' that implements Fourier synthesis directly in hardware — each oscillator has independently controllable frequency, phase, and amplitude. This massively parallel approach enables real-time audio synthesis without software overhead, capable of emulating various synthesis techniques and demonstrated as an 80-voice polyphonic synthesizer.

recent_posts.title: DIY RGB laser vector projector with ESP32 plays Asteroids and projects SVGs
recent_posts.summary: A well-documented, low-cost RGB laser vector projector built by Breq and Mia using AliExpress galvanometers, an RGB laser module with dichroic mirrors, and an ESP32-S2 microcontroller. The ESP32-S2's built-in DAC pair drives the galvos directly, enabling vector graphics, SVG projection, a clock, text rendering, and even a playable Asteroids game with Wiimote controllers. The project emphasizes safety (ANSI-certified glasses were the most expensive component) and thorough documentation explaining design decisions, making it a strong starting point for anyone interested in DIY laser projection.

recent_posts.title: Google silently installed a 4GB LLM in Chrome and users didn't consent
recent_posts.summary: Google has quietly bundled a 4GB Gemini Nano LLM into Chrome without user consent, causing performance slowdowns and disk activity for billions of users. The author argues this sets a troubling precedent where software silently installs resource-hungry AI models users can't control or opt out of. Drawing a parallel to Microsoft's Clippy, the piece calls for local LLMs to be opt-in, user-controlled applications rather than hidden components — and suggests tools like llama.cpp represent a healthier model where users own their AI and their data.

recent_posts.title: How To Better Enjoy VR On Linux
recent_posts.summary: WayVR is an open-source project that enables Linux users to control their desktop and launch applications from within a VR session. Unlike existing solutions such as WiVRn that only stream VR content to standalone headsets, WayVR allows full desktop interaction — clicking, typing, and launching apps — using a VR headset and controllers. This significantly improves the usability of Linux in VR environments and opens up experimentation in VR user interfaces.
